     leader  ---- streaming replication ---->  replicas

* only with --pgbouncer

#How a client finds the leader

  1. The load balancer calls GET /primary on port 8008 of each node.
  2. Patroni answers 200 only on the leader.
  3. The load balancer sends port 5432 traffic only to the node that answers 200.
  4. For port 5433 the load balancer calls GET /replica. Only healthy replicas answer 200.

The check runs each 5 seconds, with a 3-second timeout and 2 retries.

#How failover works

  1. Each Patroni holds or watches a leader key in etcd. The key expires after 30 seconds (ttl).
  2. If the leader stops, its key expires.
  3. A replica takes the key and promotes its Postgres to leader.
  4. The load balancer health check finds the new leader.
  5. Clients must connect again. Open connections to the old leader are lost.

etcd needs 2 of 3 members to work. The cluster continues when one node is down. It does not continue when two nodes are down.

With --monitor, each node also runs pgha-monitor.timer. Read section 20.

#Redis on the same nodes

With Redis, each node also runs Redis, Sentinel and a small role check. A Redis-only cluster runs these and no Postgres, Patroni or etcd.

                 +-----------------------------+
                 |   Hetzner Load Balancer     |   health check:
                 |   :6379  Redis read-write   |   HTTP :8009 on each node
                 |   :6380  Redis read-only    |   (/redis/primary, /redis/replica)
                 +--------------+--------------+
                                |
+----------------+      +----------------+      +----------------+
| <name>-pg1     |      | <name>-pg2     |      | <name>-pg3     |
| Redis     6379 |      | Redis     6379 |      | Redis     6379 |
| Sentinel 26379 |      | Sentinel 26379 |      | Sentinel 26379 |
| check     8009 |      | check     8009 |      | check     8009 |
+----------------+      +----------------+      +----------------+
     primary ---- asynchronous replication ---->  replicas
  1. The role check on port 8009 answers 200 on /redis/primary only on the primary, and on /redis/replica only on a replica whose link to the primary is up.
  2. When the primary stops answering for 5 seconds, a majority of the Sentinels agree and promote a replica. The others follow it.
  3. The load balancer finds the new primary with its health check. A Sentinel-aware client finds it at once.

Sentinel needs a majority of the nodes, like etcd. Read section 16.
